skill.displayName: Nano Banana Pro 精准文字图片

version.changelog: Rewritten with copy-locking, five runnable text-image workflows, and character-level verification.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its image-generation purpose, but it handles API keys and file transfers with overly broad endpoint controls that could expose credentials or selected files if misconfigured or pointed at an untrusted server.

dimensions.detail: Network access, selected-file upload, and result download are expected for this skill, but arbitrary base-url support, unvalidated server-provided upload/download destinations, and unbounded result downloads are broader than the task requires and create credential, file, and disk-use risk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a simple unpinned pip install of requests plus an init command that opens the AI Hive site and writes an API key config; there is no evidence of privilege escalation or hidden installer behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The user-facing instructions explain image generation, manual review, API setup, routing, and output directories, but they do not clearly warn that the API base URL can be changed and will receive the bearer API key, or that upload/download URLs returned by the service are trusted without destination or size validation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists the AI Hive API key in ~/.ai-hive/config.json and tightens permissions to 0600; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but users should treat the stored key as a long-lived credential. No system service, scheduler, shell hook, or cross-session backdoor was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented workflow is for exact-text image generation with human character-by-character review, and the executed skill CLI fixes generation to the Nano Banana Pro image model; however, the shipped script also contains broader generic AI Hive client code for chat, video, model listing, and user-info functions that are not needed for the stated skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust AI Hive and will keep the default API endpoint. Do not pass a custom --base-url or set AI_HIVE_BASE_URL unless you control and trust that endpoint, because it can receive your API key. Upload only files you intend to send to the service, use a limited-scope API key if available, and monitor output downloads for unexpectedly large files.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the artifact does not implement automated text verification, but SKILL.md explicitly instructs manual character review and warns that non-tolerant price, legal, medical, or terms text should be laid out separately in design software.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Partly accepted: the script includes broader generic AI Hive functions than the image-only purpose needs, but the __main__ skill parser exposes only generate, task, upload, and init.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Downgraded: video-generation functions and a generic parser are present in the file, but direct execution runs skill_main, whose CLI does not expose a video subcommand.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Downgraded: user-info and model-listing methods exist; model listing is used internally for pricing/model lookup, while user-info is not exposed through the executed skill CLI.
[LP3] expected: Network calls, selected-file reads, downloads, and config writes are expected for an API-backed image skill, but endpoint and transfer scoping is under-disclosed.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad image-text activation wording matches the skill's intended use for posters, social covers, bilingual visuals, and e-commerce images; this is not treated as a standalone security issue.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-language docs and CLI text are apparent from the artifact and align with the described Chinese text-image workflow; this is user-experience scope, not evidence of malicious behavior.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: --base-url, AI_HIVE_BASE_URL, and config base_url can point authenticated requests at any origin, sending the API key as a bearer token without host or scheme validation.
[T09] expected: Partly accepted: service-provided upload and download URLs are part of the workflow, but the code does not validate destinations, methods, redirects, or maximum download size.
[T08] expected: The requests dependency is expected for this Python API client, but the install instruction is unpinned and therefore less reproducible.
